chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hamid, from Walid ibn Sabih, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Gold for gold, and silver for silver; the excess (fadl) between them is the prohibited usury (riba).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging gold for gold with an excess amount?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the mechanism of *riba al-fadl* by specifying that when exchanging like commodities (gold for gold or silver for silver), any excess amount constitutes the prohibited usury. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on exact equality in weight or measure to preserve economic justice and prevent hidden exploitation in trade. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the specific conditions under which surplus in identical goods is deemed invalid.
